Compare the models

48 test rows · log loss: lower is better. Table order is descriptive; the primary model is unchanged.

CV choice: Logistic regressionLogistic regression was selected using 5-fold cross-validation on the training rows. 15 settings were tried; one fitted representative per successful family is kept here.Inspect the searchScore definitionslog loss: Probability error that penalizes confident wrong answers; lower is better. Brier score: Mean squared error of the positive-class probability, from 0 (best) to 1 (worst); lower is better. binned calibration gap: Average absolute gap between grouped probabilities and observed frequencies; lower is better, but the value depends on the evaluation sample and grouping. accuracy: Share of evaluation rows assigned to the correct class; higher is better. balanced accuracy: Average recall across the positive and negative classes; higher is better. Unavailable when either class is absent from the evaluation rows. ROC AUC: Chance that a random positive receives a higher score than a random negative; higher is better.

Performance vs cost Left means lower measured cost. For a loss such as RMSE or log loss, lower is better; for accuracy or R-squared, higher is better. Outlined models are not beaten on both axes. Single-fit millisecond timings are descriptive readings, not reliable speed rankings.

Linear spacing compares absolute cost differences. Log spacing compares ratios: 1 to 10 uses the same space as 10 to 100. It can separate inexpensive models when one model is much larger or slower. All plotted costs must be positive; scores and the Pareto frontier do not change.
Log spacing compares ratios between positive losses. It can separate useful models when one alternative has a much larger error. All models and their original scores remain visible. Zero losses and scores such as accuracy or R-squared use a linear axis.

Linear cost axis. Scale switching requires JavaScript.

How costs were measured

Times are measured on this machine. Fit time covers the retained fit, not the entire cross-validation search; prediction time covers this evaluation batch. A displayed ~0 means no elapsed time was recorded; timer resolution varies by platform. It does not mean the operation takes no time. Size is an approximate R object measurement, not a count of learned rules. These measurements are not hardware-independent benchmarks.

Measure repeated prediction costs

A single timer reading can be too coarse for small models. Measure repeated predictions on a common batch to compare their costs.

bench <- benchmark_predictions(result)
render_model_report(result, "report.html", benchmark = bench)

Neural network: search rationale

Small single-layer networks and several weight penalties bound the search cost. Numeric inputs and regression outcomes are standardized using each training fold. The default 2,000-iteration cap gives difficult fits more time; converged fits stop early. Changing only maxit preserves initialization, and nonconverged fits remain excluded by default. 7 of 12 available tuples scheduled; 5 untested.

Preset values are package choices, not data-optimized ranges.

Tested: size: 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 · decay: 0.1, 0.03, 0.001, 0.01 · maxit: 2000

Decision tree: search rationale

Preset tuples move from shallow trees and larger minimum splits toward deeper trees. Minimum split sizes are fractions of outer-training row count, bounded below by four. 7 of 12 available tuples scheduled; 5 untested.

Preset values are package choices, not data-optimized ranges.

Exact selection arithmetic and preference order

Eligible loss ≤ 0.506611 + 0.017591 = 0.524202. Among eligible candidates: first the preferred family, then its smallest recorded capacity proxy, then score and configuration ID to break a tie.

Values: Family, Preference order, Within-family capacity proxy
FamilyPreference orderWithin-family capacity proxy
Logistic regression1potential coefficient count
Decision tree4within-family potential leaf count
Neural network9within-family connection count

Family order is package or user preference. Capacity proxies omit some regularization controls; they do not establish a universal least-flexible model.

CV loss is averaged across validation rows, weighting folds by their evaluated row counts. Fold-score SE is a selection heuristic. Training folds overlap; it is not a confidence interval, equivalence test or population uncertainty.

Preprocessing was learned again inside every fold. The evaluation partition was not used to choose hyperparameters. Full fold assignments and any retained out-of-fold predictions remain in tuning_results(result).

Why this grid? Coverage, parameter meaning and boundary winners

Round-robin ordered grid prefixes; explicit family budgets override the total allocation. Outer training rows: 192; raw inputs: 3.

Exact preset numbers are package engineering choices, not values justified as optimal by literature. This finite joint-configuration search does not identify causal effects of individual settings.

Recorded search budget and rationale
FamilyGrid sourceAvailable tuplesScheduled tuplesUntested tuplesRationale
linearpackage_presets110One unpenalized reference fit; there is no parameter grid for this family.
treepackage_presets1275Preset tuples move from shallow trees and larger minimum splits toward deeper trees. Minimum split sizes are fractions of outer-training row count, bounded below by four.
neuralpackage_presets1275Small single-layer networks and several weight penalties bound the search cost. Numeric inputs and regression outcomes are standardized using each training fold. The default 2,000-iteration cap gives difficult fits more time; converged fits stop early. Changing only maxit preserves initialization, and nonconverged fits remain excluded by default.
Available values and parameter meanings
FamilyParameterAvailable preset valuesMeaning
treemaxdepth2, 4, 6, 10, 3, 5, 8Maximum permitted tree depth, not observed depth.
treecp0.03, 0.01, 0.003, 0.0005, 0.001, 0Larger thresholds discourage small-improvement splits.
treeminsplit38, 23, 15, 10, 6, 4Minimum training rows in a node before attempting a split.
neuralsize1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16Hidden units in one layer; more units permit more patterns.
neuraldecay0.1, 0.03, 0.01, 0.001, 0, 0.0001Weight penalty; larger values discourage large weights.
neuralmaxit2000Optimizer iteration limit. It can stop earlier; a larger limit does not guarantee convergence.
Position of each family CV winner within scheduled numeric settings

A fixed setting was not varied. An edge winner can motivate a new training-only comparison; it does not show that extending one control would help, because several controls may differ between the tested tuples.

Copy and change this search grid in R

This executable control reproduces the scheduled tuples and budgets. Edit a tuple to test a specific hypothesis. Refit using your original data, preprocessing, validation design and seed. This control alone does not reproduce the entire analysis. Avoid repeatedly tuning against the evaluation partition.

control <- tuning_control(
  grids = list(linear = list(list()), tree = list(list(maxdepth = 2L, cp = 0.03,
    minsplit = 38L), list(maxdepth = 4L, cp = 0.01, minsplit = 23L),
    list(maxdepth = 6L, cp = 0.003, minsplit = 15L), list(maxdepth = 10L,
        cp = 5e-04, minsplit = 10L), list(maxdepth = 3L, cp = 0.01,
        minsplit = 38L), list(maxdepth = 5L, cp = 0.003, minsplit = 15L),
    list(maxdepth = 8L, cp = 0.001, minsplit = 10L)), neural = list(
    list(size = 1L, decay = 0.1, maxit = 2000L), list(size = 2L,
        decay = 0.03, maxit = 2000L), list(size = 4L, decay = 0.01,
        maxit = 2000L), list(size = 6L, decay = 0.01, maxit = 2000L),
    list(size = 8L, decay = 0.001, maxit = 2000L), list(size = 2L,
        decay = 0.001, maxit = 2000L), list(size = 4L, decay = 0.001,
        maxit = 2000L))),
  family_budgets = c(linear = 1L, tree = 7L, neural = 7L),
  metric = "log_loss",
  optimization_policy = "exclude",
  family_priority = c("linear", "tree", "neural")
)
# In your original autoxplain(...) call, use:
#   learners = c("linear", "tree", "neural"), max_models = NULL, tuning_control = control
#   tuning_rule = "one_se", seed = 33
# Keep the original preprocessing and validation design (including supplied fold IDs).

Use tuning_evidence(result) for the aggregate record.

Features

Feature importance & effectsALE follows local changes in predictions and centers the effect at zero. Negative effects mean below this reference, not negative probabilities. PDP averages predictions with an input set to each displayed value. These describe fitted associations, not the consequences of an intervention.

Do the models disagree?

48 evaluation rows · 3 models · declared reference excluded. These are descriptive differences among the included models, not confidence intervals. A weak model can disagree with a strong one; compare their scores before treating a gap as useful evidence. Class decisions here use the recorded event class and a fixed 0.50 cutoff.

Diagnostic coverage and association evidence

evaluation: computed. Ordered observations, outcomes and event semantics agree; independence and representativeness are not established by these checks.

association: computed. Limited pairwise screen: absolute Spearman correlation for numeric pairs, correlation ratio for mixed pairs, and Cramer's V for categorical pairs. Small values do not establish independence or exclude nonlinear or joint dependence. Categorical pairs without repeated categories are unavailable; many rare categories can inflate association.

permutation: computed. Loss changes describe these shuffles. The intervals quantify shuffle randomness, not sampling, fitting or selection uncertainty.

comparison: insufficient evidence. Fewer than two supplied models meet the performance tolerance.

resources: computed.

model_behavior: computed.

prediction_disagreement: computed.

decision_cutoffs: computed.

Interval method and assumptions

Paired percentile intervals conditional on the fitted models, from 1000 bootstrap draws. These intervals omit fitting and selection uncertainty and assume independent sampling units.

Training settings

What do these settings mean?

Training controls and learned parameter values are different. maxdepth caps the number of splits along a path; minsplit is the minimum rows considered for a split; minbucket is the minimum rows in a leaf. cp sets a minimum relative improvement for splitting. Metric definitions
Definitions for every metric
log loss
Probability error that penalizes confident wrong answers; lower is better.
Brier score
Mean squared error of the positive-class probability, from 0 (best) to 1 (worst); lower is better.
binned calibration gap
Average absolute gap between grouped probabilities and observed frequencies; lower is better, but the value depends on the evaluation sample and grouping.
accuracy
Share of evaluation rows assigned to the correct class; higher is better.
balanced accuracy
Average recall across the positive and negative classes; higher is better. Unavailable when either class is absent from the evaluation rows.
ROC AUC
Chance that a random positive receives a higher score than a random negative; higher is better.

Reading this analysis

Scores describe the recorded evaluation split. Feature effects describe fitted associations. Use independent evaluation data for a final assessment after changing models or predictors. Neither this report nor a passing diagnostic establishes causal effects.
